title: Mail Composer - Email Composition and Delivery
text: Reply existing conversation: Note: gm_create_draft() support thread_id. Drafts always standalone, mc_draft() warns pass one. Use mc_send() deliver straight thread, send draft manually Gmail UI (Gmail match subject line starts “Re:”).
code: # Find the thread mc_thread_find("from:brandon subject:cottonwood")  # Read the conversation to review context mc_thread_read("19c05f0a98188c91")  # Include drafts in the thread (adds a status column: "sent" / "draft") mc_thread_read("19c05f0a98188c91", drafts = TRUE)  # Send into it mc_send("draft.md",         to = "brandon@example.com",         subject = "Re: Cottonwood plugs",         thread_id = "19c05f0a98188c91")

title: Mail Composer - Email Composition and Delivery
text: Send email later send_at — either minutes now specific time. Use scheduler = "auto" durable OS-native scheduling (recommended): scheduler argument selects backend: "callr" (default backward compatibility) — callr::r_bg background R process. Survives session lifecycles can cleaned parent context exits (one-shot Rscript -e, RStudio sessions close, CI). Emits warning() use steering toward "auto". "auto" — resolves launchd macOS Linux. OS-native daemon owns job lifecycle independent R session — survives shell exit, parent process death, (macOS) sleep/wake cycles. "launchd" / "" — force specific backend. Heartbeat log entries land ~/.mc/send_log.txt missed fires auditable log alone: SCHEDULED submission target time STARTED fire, just actual send SENT / SKIPPED / FAILED outcome SCHEDULED line follow-STARTED means bg process died firing — failure mode OS-native backends solve. macOS, caffeinate keeps machine awake email sends (callr backend — launchd handles wake/sleep ). machine sleeps send window callr backend, 5-minute grace period applies — past , send skipped prevent stale emails. Outcomes also trigger macOS desktop notification success, skip, failure.
code: # Send in 10 minutes via launchd (macOS) or atd (Linux) mc_send("draft.md",         to = "brandon@example.com",         subject = "Cottonwood plugs",         send_at = 10,         scheduler = "auto")  # Send at a specific time mc_send("draft.md",         to = "brandon@example.com",         subject = "Cottonwood plugs",         send_at = as.POSIXct("2026-02-24 09:11:00"),         scheduler = "auto")

title: Build and deliver a message (internal) — mc_deliver
text: path Path markdown draft file. Passed mc_md_render(). Recipient email address (character string vector). subject Email subject line. cc Optional CC recipients (character vector). Default NULL. bcc Optional BCC recipients (character vector). Default NULL. Sender address. Default uses getOption("mc."), MC_FROM environment variable. Errors neither set. thread_id Gmail thread ID reply . Default NULL (new thread). Use mc_thread_find() look thread IDs. .draft Logical. TRUE creates Gmail draft, FALSE sends. Supplied wrapper, never caller. to_self Logical. TRUE, override drop cc, bcc thread_id, message reaches nobody sender. Default FALSE. caps receives message; stop send. Use mc_draft() want message delivered . sig Logical. Append signature? Passed mc_md_render(). Default TRUE. sig_path Path custom signature HTML file. Default NULL uses bundled New Graph signature. Passed mc_md_render(). Ignored sig = FALSE html provided. attachments Optional character vector file paths attach. file attached via gmailr::gm_attach_file(). Default NULL. labels Optional character vector Gmail label names apply resulting thread. Applied via mc_thread_modify() successful send. labels_create Logical. TRUE (default), missing user labels labels auto-created via mc_label_ensure(). html Optional pre-rendered HTML body. provided, path ignored HTML used directly. send_at Schedule email later. Either POSIXct datetime numeric number minutes now. Default NULL (send now). Scheduling inherently send, lives mc_draft(). scheduler Backend scheduled send. One "callr" (default), "auto" (OS-native: launchd macOS, Linux), "launchd", "". Ignored send_at NULL.

title: Send an email from a markdown file — mc_send
text: path Path markdown draft file. Passed mc_md_render(). Recipient email address (character string vector). subject Email subject line. cc Optional CC recipients (character vector). Default NULL. bcc Optional BCC recipients (character vector). Default NULL. Sender address. Default uses getOption("mc."), MC_FROM environment variable. Errors neither set. thread_id Gmail thread ID reply . Default NULL (new thread). Use mc_thread_find() look thread IDs. to_self Logical. TRUE, override drop cc, bcc thread_id, message reaches nobody sender. Default FALSE. caps receives message; stop send. Use mc_draft() want message delivered . sig Logical. Append signature? Passed mc_md_render(). Default TRUE. sig_path Path custom signature HTML file. Default NULL uses bundled New Graph signature. Passed mc_md_render(). Ignored sig = FALSE html provided. attachments Optional character vector file paths attach. file attached via gmailr::gm_attach_file(). Default NULL. labels Optional character vector Gmail label names apply resulting thread. Applied via mc_thread_modify() successful send. labels_create Logical. TRUE (default), missing user labels labels auto-created via mc_label_ensure(). html Optional pre-rendered HTML body. provided, path ignored HTML used directly. send_at Schedule email later. Either POSIXct datetime numeric number minutes now. Default NULL (send now). Scheduling inherently send, lives mc_draft(). scheduler Backend scheduled send. One "callr" (default), "auto" (OS-native: launchd macOS, Linux), "launchd", "". Ignored send_at NULL.

title: mc 0.2.10
text: mc_send() gains scheduler argument selecting backend scheduled sends — "callr" (default, backward compatibility), "auto" (resolves OS-native: launchd macOS, Linux), explicit "launchd" / "". OS-native backends job lifecycle independent originating R session — fixes silent-drop failure mode callr::r_bg child got cleaned parent Rscript invocation exited (#36). Behavior change: using scheduler = "callr" now emits warning() flagging unreliable lifecycle call contexts (Rscript one-shot, RStudio sessions exit, CI). Steers users toward scheduler = "auto". default still "callr" back-compat — pass scheduler = "auto" (set YAML override) silence warning use OS-native backend. send_at now writes heartbeat log entries ~/.mc/send_log.txt missed fires auditable log alone: SCHEDULED submission target time, STARTED fire, plus existing SENT / SKIPPED / FAILED entries. SCHEDULED line follow-STARTED means bg process died firing (#36). Internal: scheduled-send HTML now pre-rendered backend dispatch body travels serialized args — avoids fire-time filesystem dependency original draft fixes potential silent failure path-based scheduled sends. Internal: new R/mc_schedule.R houses dispatcher, backends, run_scheduled_send fire-time entry point used OS-native backends. Triple-colon access pattern matches existing internal helpers. Internal: launchd cleanup unlinks plist + args JSON without calling launchctl unload inside running job — unload SIGTERMs job’s process group, killing cleanup mid-flight (caught live test). Stale launchctl list entry persists next reboot dormant StartCalendarInterval (set single past minute) never re-fires.

title: mc 0.2.9

System labels (INBOX, STARRED, etc.) skipped via case-insensitive match (#33). mc_thread_modify() gains create_missing = FALSE (opt-). TRUE, calls mc_label_ensure(add) resolving names new labels add auto-created. Default preserves existing typo-guard behavior (#33). mc_send() gains labels_create = TRUE (default ). YAML- driven workflow (mc_md_send()) now creates new project tags first use — need pre-create labels via gmailr::gm_create_label(). Set FALSE strict typo-guard. Threaded scheduled-send recursion (#33). Internal: resolve_label_names() now matches system labels case- insensitively normalizes returned IDs uppercase, fixing cross-function inconsistency mc_label_ensure skipped "inbox" system mc_thread_modify erred trying resolve . Side benefit: callers can pass mixed-case system labels (“Inbox”, “Starred”) get correct resolution.
